newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes mid-range after sluggish session.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes mid-range after sluggish session.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended about the middle of its range on Thursday after a sluggish and rather directionless session.
It ended at 5.00 p.m. (0500 GMT) at US$0.6923/30, down from its 0.6938 high, but up on its 0.6912/19 opening. The Trade-Weighted Index was up at 68.12 from 68.04.

Dealers weren't disappointed in their expectation that the kiwi would rebound after it had been shunted half a cent lower by comments on Wednesday from Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash that it was overvalued.
While it had partially recovered, traders said the range had slipped a notch lower to 0.6900-40 range.

"It still seems to be struggling. I think it would need a push above 0.6950 to encourage people back into the kiwi, although there does seem to bids when we get down to the high 68s (cents)," a dealer said.
He said the kiwi had appeared to get stuck in a rut again with Wednesday's lows unlikely to be seen again for a couple of days.
There was little on the local news agenda to give it fresh impetus and any direction was most likely to come from Tuesday's FOMC meeting where the market is expecting a rise in official U.S. rates.
